source.version: Published journal article, Batı Anadolu Eğitim Bilimleri Dergisi / Western Anatolia Journal of Educational Sciences, 2026, 17(1), 70-93; published 28 April 2026; DOI 10.51460/baebd.1757062 (PDF p. 1, printed p. 70, publication information).
source.title_on_document: ChatGPT Destekli Dönütlerin İlkokul Öğrencilerinin Yaratıcı Yazma Becerilerine Etkisi

supplement.where: Included Appendices Ek 1, Ek 2 and Ek 3, PDF pp. 22-24 (printed pp. 91-93). No separate external supplement is stated.
supplement.holds: Examples of student texts from the intervention weeks, examples labelled as post-test student texts, and example ChatGPT texts. These are illustrative images, not additional statistical tables. Means, standard deviations, t-tests and reported eta/eta-squared are in the main text, Tables 6-8 (PDF pp. 15-16, printed pp. 84-85).

paper_design_summary: Two third-grade classes in a public school in Van were assigned by drawing class names from a bag: the first drawn class received the ChatGPT-supported intervention and the next drawn class was the control (PDF p. 8, printed p. 77, Study group). During six weeks, the intervention class examined teacher-presented AI example stories, received teacher/peer feedback and rewrote its own texts; the control class wrote and shared stories without the additional feedback or creative-writing instruction (PDF pp. 9, 11-13, printed pp. 78, 80-82, ChatGPT and Data collection). The researcher scored individual pre-test and week-8 post-test stories with a creative-writing rubric, analyzing 30 pupils per arm; the schedule lists AI support during weeks 2-7 and only story writing and assessment at post-test (PDF pp. 11-12 and 15, printed pp. 80-81 and 84, Table 4 and Table 6).

studies.label: Third-grade creative-writing instruction and subsequent story-writing test

assignment.what_was_assigned: Class-level allocation in ordinary school instruction: names of the school's eight third-grade classes were placed in a bag; the first drawn class was assigned to the intervention and the next to control. There was one class per arm. The school was selected by convenience. Although the author calls the design quasi-experimental, the described lottery explicitly determines treatment assignment; individuals were not separately randomized.
assignment.quote: Okulda bulunan sekiz 3. Sınıf şubelerinin isimleri ayrı kâğıtlara yazılarak bir torbaya atılmış; ilk seçilen şube deney grubu, seçilen bir sonraki şube ise kontrol grubu olarak atanmıştır.
assignment.locator: PDF p. 8 (printed p. 77), Çalışma grubu / Study group, class-lottery paragraph; author's quasi-experimental label: PDF p. 7 (printed p. 76), Araştırmanın modeli / Research model.

arms.name: ChatGPT examples plus teacher-guided feedback and rewriting
arms.description: Pupils wrote stories, shared them and received peer feedback; the teacher generated a story on the same theme with ChatGPT, led comparison of the example with student work, and supported rewriting and instruction on creative-writing elements. Students did not use ChatGPT individually (PDF p. 9, printed p. 78, ChatGPT; PDF pp. 11-12, printed pp. 80-81, Data collection and Table 4).

arms.name: Paper-and-pencil creative writing without additional feedback
arms.description: Pupils wrote on the same weekly topics and shared their texts in class. The teacher gave no written/oral feedback or additional creative-writing instruction beyond the standard lesson (PDF pp. 12-13, printed pp. 81-82, Data collection).

participants.exclusions: After the classes had been designated intervention/control, initial general-writing work and classroom-teacher judgments led to exclusion of data for 4 intervention pupils and 5 control pupils with low writing skills, before the creative-writing pre-test (PDF pp. 10-11, printed pp. 79-80, Data collection). Tables 6-7 subsequently report 30 analyzed pupils per arm. The original numbers at class assignment are not stated, so no randomized people count is inferred. No additional numerical attrition count is reported.
participants.who: Third-grade pupils at one public school in the İpekyolu district of Van province during the 2024-2025 school year. The analyzed sample is 30 intervention pupils and 30 control pupils (PDF p. 3, printed p. 72, Extended Abstract, Method; PDF p. 8, printed p. 77, Table 1; PDF p. 15, printed p. 84, Tables 6-7).
participants.quote: Araştırmanın çalışma grubu, Van ilinde devlet okullarının birinde 3. sınıfta öğrenimine devam eden 60 öğrenciden oluşmaktadır.
participants.locator: PDF p. 8 (printed p. 77), Study group and Table 1; PDF p. 15 (printed p. 84), Tables 6-7, analyzed N; PDF p. 11 (printed p. 80), Data collection, exclusions; PDF p. 3 (printed p. 72), Extended Abstract, Method, district and school year.

ai_tool.name_model: ChatGPT, GPT-3.5, accessed through the OpenAI website, as stated in the paper (PDF p. 9, printed p. 78, ChatGPT).
ai_tool.how_used: The teacher requested an example story on the same theme as the pupils' stories and displayed it on the classroom electronic board. The class compared content, structure and expression under teacher guidance, then pupils revised their own texts. AI generated examples; the teacher and peers provided feedback. Pupils did not directly interact with ChatGPT, and no individualized student-specific content was generated (PDF p. 9, printed p. 78, ChatGPT; PDF p. 12, printed p. 81, Data collection).

task.description: Story writing using word lists and imaginative prompts. The pre-test required a story using homeland, flag, soldier, friendship and village; the post-test required each pupil to use budget, family, shopping, need, wish and help. Intervention exercises also included imaginary characters, what-if prompts and collaborative stories; the scored pre/post products were individual stories (PDF p. 10, printed p. 79, Table 3; PDF p. 11, printed p. 80, Data collection).
task.duration: Six intervention weeks, one day per week with three lessons of 40+40+40 minutes; eight weeks including the pre-test in week 1 and post-test in week 8. The pre-test writing task is explicitly allotted 40 minutes; a separate post-test time limit is not stated (PDF pp. 11-12, printed pp. 80-81, Data collection and Table 4).

outcomes.name: Creative Writing Products Evaluation Scale total score at post-test
outcomes.question: after_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: The researcher scored the pupils' stories with Kasap's Creative Writing Products Evaluation Scale: a unidimensional 24-item rubric, each item scored 1-5, total range 24-120 (PDF p. 8, printed p. 77, Data collection tools; PDF p. 11, printed p. 80, Data collection). The rater was the academic researcher, not a crowd panel; blinding and an independent second rater are not stated. Table 2 presents low, moderate, good and advanced performance bands of the same total score, and the results describe counts in these bands; these are retained as an alternative presentation of the same outcome rather than a separate outcome (PDF p. 9, printed p. 78, Table 2; PDF p. 15, printed p. 84, results below Table 6). The reported analyses use pupil-level independent and paired t-tests, with no stated adjustment for class-level assignment (PDF p. 13, printed p. 82, Data analysis; PDF p. 15, printed p. 84, Tables 6-7).
outcomes.delay: Post-test in week 8, a later test week after the intervention in weeks 2-7; exact elapsed days since the last AI-supported lesson are not stated. The procedure table lists ChatGPT only during the intervention and story writing plus scoring for both arms at post-test (PDF p. 12, printed p. 81, Table 4; PDF p. 11, printed p. 80, Data collection).

contrasts.treatment_arm: ChatGPT examples plus teacher-guided feedback and rewriting
contrasts.control_arm: Paper-and-pencil creative writing without additional feedback
contrasts.reported: Post-test (Table 6): experimental N = 30, mean = 73,40, S = 24,61; control N = 30, mean = 40,23, S = 11,33; df = 58, t = 6.705, p = .000. Post-test effect-size table (Table 8): η = .771; η² = .594. Numbers and decimal punctuation are retained as printed; p = .000 is the printed value. The reported standardized-effect entry is eta/eta-squared, not a computed standardized mean difference. No confidence interval or standard error is printed.
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 15 (printed p. 84), Table 6, post-test rows; PDF p. 16 (printed p. 85), Table 8.

sample_overlap.shares_participants_with: Not stated. The paper describes original school data collection; it does not identify reuse of another paper's participants.
sample_overlap.locator: PDF pp. 8 and 10-11 (printed pp. 77 and 79-80), Study group and Data collection.

company_involvement.description: No company authorship, funding or research involvement is stated. The author is affiliated with Van Yüzüncü Yıl University; OpenAI is named as the provider of the ChatGPT website.
company_involvement.locator: PDF p. 1 (printed p. 70), author affiliation; PDF p. 9 (printed p. 78), ChatGPT.

eligibility.reason: The paper explicitly describes a lottery allocating intact classes to the AI-supported and no-AI conditions: first class drawn to intervention, next to control (PDF p. 8, printed p. 77, Study group). This supports class-randomized field_rct coding despite the author's quasi-experimental label (PDF p. 7, printed p. 76, Research model). Tables 6-7 analyze 60 people, 30 per arm (PDF p. 15, printed p. 84), meeting the people threshold. The researcher scores students' story products on a creative-writing rubric (PDF pp. 8 and 11, printed pp. 77 and 80, Data collection tools and Data collection). The outcome is coded after_ai from the separate week-8 test after AI-supported instruction in weeks 2-7 (PDF p. 12, printed p. 81, Table 4). Eligibility does not establish usable pooled precision: only one class per arm was allocated, and the paper reports pupil-level tests without class adjustment.

one_line_finding: Among 60 analyzed pupils, post-test creative-writing means were 73,40 after ChatGPT-supported instruction versus 40,23 after control instruction, with t(58) = 6.705 and p = .000 as printed (PDF p. 15, printed p. 84, Table 6).
open_questions: Starting class sizes are not stated: the paper reports excluding 4 intervention pupils and 5 control pupils, yet the analyzed tables contain 30 pupils per arm; the number of people at assignment cannot be confirmed (PDF p. 11, printed p. 80, Data collection; PDF p. 15, printed p. 84, Tables 6-7).

Post-test AI absence is coded from Table 4, which limits ChatGPT to weeks 2-7 and lists only story writing and scoring at week 8. The prose does not separately state an explicit prohibition on AI or feedback during the post-test, and the exact delay in days is not given (PDF pp. 11-12, printed pp. 80-81).

The control post-test S is 11,33 in Table 6 and 11,31 in Table 7. Table 7 lists df = 29 for paired tests, whereas the prose on the next page prints t(30); these inconsistencies remain unresolved (PDF pp. 15-16, printed pp. 84-85).

No uncertainty estimate adjusted for the randomized classes is reported; pupil-level t-tests do not account for the assignment unit (PDF p. 8, printed p. 77, class lottery; PDF pp. 13 and 15, printed pp. 82 and 84, Data analysis and Tables 6-7).
notes: Screened against the full markdown, including all appendices, and checked the PDF pages for design, counts, measures and recorded statistics on 2026-10-09. PDF-page locators are one-based and are accompanied by printed page numbers. The author calls this a quasi-experiment, but the explicit ordered lottery assigns the conditions; convenience school selection is a separate issue (PDF pp. 7-8, printed pp. 76-77). The intervention combines AI examples with teacher/peer feedback, revision and creative-writing instruction, while the control lacks the additional feedback/instruction. The author explicitly acknowledges that the contribution of ChatGPT cannot be separated from receiving feedback generally (PDF p. 16, printed p. 85, Discussion). Baseline descriptive context in Table 6: experimental N = 30, mean = 34,23, S = 14,56; control N = 30, mean = 35,66, S = 10,82; df = 58, t = -.433, p = .667 (PDF p. 15, printed p. 84). Table 7 reports the same pre/post means and intervention SDs, with paired-test df = 29, t = -7.887, p = .000 for intervention, and df = 29, t = -8.238, p = .000 for control; its control post-test S is 11,31 (PDF p. 15, printed p. 84). Table 7 is headed as a Shapiro-Wilk analysis despite displaying pre/post means, S, t and p; its df also conflicts with the adjacent narrative, so printed table values are retained without correction. These are repeated analyses of the same creativity score, not additional outcomes. No effect size was computed. A preparatory pilot in another third-grade class is mentioned only to establish feasibility and lesson duration; it supplies no participant count or comparative scored outcome and is not counted as a second evidence study (PDF p. 11, printed p. 80, Data collection). No preregistration or public data/code URL is stated.
